messages.subject: EAPsum and a mix of dichotomous and three level items.
messages.subject_clean: EAPsum and a mix of dichotomous and three level items.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil and Group Members,

So, working on a performance scale (i.e., there are wrong and right answers) that has a mix of dichotomous scored items (right , wrong) and 3-level scored items (right, kind of right, wrong) I have been using mirt to estimate 1 factor models  itemtype = "graded". Now, the items are coded as 0,1,2 and 0,2 to denote that in the dichotomous items there is no half credit answer. mirt() recodes the 2 into 1 and estimates only b1 for those items. So far so good because it becomes equivalent to a 2PL difficulty parameter b.

During the exercise of analysing this instrument I attempted to create EAPsum scores. The problem is that our mirt model objects have recoded the 2 point scores of the dichotmous items into 1... so when it ads up instead of having a potential score between 0 and 2xnumber of items, the maximum potential score is number of dichotomous items + 2 x number of three-level scored items. Therefore this new recoded score cannot be compared to a raw score where all items have a 2 point score.

Question... and probably I will try that... could that be fixed by recoding 1 to 0.5 and 2 as 1 in the original metric? Can mirt use 0.5 scores as denoting a mid point?

Creating a lookup table using EAP with all possible patterns becomes prohibitive as the number of items pass a dozen or so.

Anyway, just one quirk I found with EAPsum and a mix bag of items.

Hope everyone is doing well. Cheers from Montreal,

Manolo Romero
@itemcinq

messages.body_plain:
Hi Manolo,

Nice to hear from you, and I hope you're staying well. Your problem sounds interesting, though I'm not certain I'd want to incorporate this into the main package source code (feel free to fork it and try it yourself though, the main driving function is located here <https://github.com/philchalmers/mirt/blob/7bf324086a08a13b777bd03a3bb8a5a9518e5bf4/R/fscores.internal.R#L763>). From what I can tell, what you be required is to trick the calcL1 function into thinking that dichotomous items are actually 3 category items, however the middle category is effectively a vector of 1's for the probability functions (e.g., cbind(P0, 1, P1)) so that the recursive updates would loop over three tracelines rather than just two. The sum score information would also need to be adjusted, and probably some other things as well to avoid finding probability products outside some plausible space (which would appear in the higher end of the total score distribution where the total scores freedom becomes limited).

That said, the look-up table is mainly an approximation anyway, and of course isn't meant to be as general as the true-blue EAP approach. Is it really so difficult to just pass the response.pattern vector to fscores()? I mean, you need all the raw scores to compute the total score anyway, so the extra step doesn't seem that bad to me....

Phil

messages.body_plain:
What you're describing is actually the purpose of the line:

COV = S1*S1, S2*S2, S3*S3

which frees the latent variances for the specific dimensions. Due to the proportionality implied by the testlet model you just need to take the estimates of these latent variables and multiply them through for the slope parameters. Hence, the within-item equality constraints are just used to imply the proportionality, while the variances of the specific factors correct for this systematic proportionality (e.g., for specific factor 2 and some given slope a2, a2* = a2 * COV_22). HTH.

Phil
